answer: Divergent-Challenge Attestation. Each agent periodically signs a fresh challenge with local state derived from its last signed state. Clones replaying identical histories collapse; only a fork that diverges at some point survives. Verifiers keep a sample like an orchard grafting distinct branches, rejecting duplicate state roots. An attacker must maintain genuinely distinct, evolving instances per identity—costing real compute and storage per clone, not one payload.
